svg.title: Stereo-PIV step by step: from camera set-up to u, v and w
svg.desc: Stereo-PIV step 1: Set up cameras and laser. Stereo-PIV step 2: Focus both cameras on the board. Stereo-PIV step 3: Lens calibration, for each camera. Stereo-PIV step 4: Board at the measurement position. Stereo-PIV step 5: Align the light sheet, record the board. Stereo-PIV step 6: Stereo calibration. Stereo-PIV step 7: Record the flow, correct the disparity. Stereo-PIV step 8: ANALYZE: from both cameras to u, v and w.
svg.text: From camera set-up to the three velocity components u, v and w
Drawings: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de · licence CC BY 4.0 (free to reuse with attribution) · PIVlab is free, open-source PIV and stereo-PIV software

svg.title: Stereo-PIV step 1: Set up cameras and laser
svg.desc: Any direction between the cameras works (30–90°). Cameras downstream of the laser see the bright forward scatter. A Scheimpflug adapter on each camera keeps the oblique view sharp everywhere. Drawing: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de, CC BY 4.0.
svg.text: Any direction between the cameras works (30–90°). Cameras downstream of the laser see the bright
forward scatter. A Scheimpflug adapter on each camera keeps the oblique view sharp everywhere.

svg.title: Stereo-PIV step 2: Focus both cameras on the board
svg.desc: Place the calibration board (generate it in PIVlab) where you will measure. Adjust focus and Scheimpflug angle until the whole board is sharp in both cameras. Tip: the Sharpness overlay of the PIVlab live image rates the left, centre and right third. Drawing: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de, CC BY 4.0.
svg.text: Focus both cameras on the board
Place the calibration board (generate it in PIVlab) where you will measure.
Adjust focus and Scheimpflug angle until the whole board is sharp in both cameras.
Tip: the Sharpness overlay of the PIVlab live image rates the left, centre and right third.

svg.title: Stereo-PIV step 3: Lens calibration, for each camera
svg.desc: Move the board through the whole image at many positions and tilts, then repeat for camera 2. No space at the measurement position? Calibrate before, then do not change focus, Scheimpflug angle or other lens settings. Drawing: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de, CC BY 4.0.
svg.text: Move the board through the whole image at many positions and tilts, then repeat for camera 2.
No space at the measurement position? Calibrate before, then do not change
focus, Scheimpflug angle or other lens settings.

svg.title: Stereo-PIV step 4: Board at the measurement position
svg.desc: The board stands exactly where you want to measure. Align the cameras so that their views overlap as much as possible; the overlap is the measurement area. The board should fill most of it. Drawing: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de, CC BY 4.0.
svg.text: The board stands exactly where you want to measure. Align the cameras so that their views overlap
as much as possible; the overlap is the measurement area. The board should fill most of it.

svg.title: Stereo-PIV step 5: Align the light sheet, record the board
svg.desc: Aim the light sheet at the board: its centre should lie on the board face (the camera side). Then switch the laser off (it grazes the board) and record the board with both cameras under normal lighting. Remove the board. From now on, the cameras must not move. Drawing: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de, CC BY 4.0.
svg.text: board images in the light sheet
Align the light sheet, record the board
Aim the light sheet at the board: its centre should lie on the board face (the camera side).
Then switch the laser off (it grazes the board) and record the board with both cameras under
normal lighting. Remove the board. From now on, the cameras must not move.

svg.title: Stereo-PIV step 6: Stereo calibration
svg.desc: PIVlab finds the board corners in both images, computes where the cameras are and maps both onto one common grid: a point of the sheet is at the same pixel in both cameras. Drawing: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de, CC BY 4.0.
svg.text: common grid in the light sheet (both cameras)
PIVlab finds the board corners in both images, computes where the cameras are and maps both
onto one common grid: a point of the sheet is at the same pixel in both cameras.

svg.title: Stereo-PIV step 7: Record the flow, correct the disparity
svg.desc: The sheet is never exactly at the board position, so the cameras place a particle at different points. Correlating camera 1 A with camera 2 A measures this map; it corrects both cameras. Drawing: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de, CC BY 4.0.
svg.text: Record the flow, correct the disparity
The sheet is never exactly at the board position, so the cameras place a particle at different points.
Correlating camera 1 A with camera 2 A measures this map; it corrects both cameras.

svg.title: Stereo-PIV step 8: ANALYZE: from both cameras to u, v and w
svg.desc: ANALYZE runs a 2D PIV analysis of each camera (same settings, corrected images). The two fields differ because each camera sees the out-of-plane motion from its own side; PIVlab combines them automatically into one 3D vector per point: u, v in the board plane, w along Z. Drawing: PIVlab, www.pivlab.de, CC BY 4.0.
svg.text: ANALYZE: from both cameras to u, v and w
ANALYZE runs a 2D PIV analysis of each camera (same settings, corrected images). The two fields
differ because each camera sees the out-of-plane motion from its own side; PIVlab combines them
automatically into one 3D vector per point: u, v in the board plane, w along Z.
